To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the MISR Version22 ANG product is improved by using the GOCART ANG as a constraint, and that the MISR version22 AAOD product is improved by constraining the AAOD to the GOCART AAOD.
the addition of GOCART aerosol properties as a constraint to the MISR retrieval improves the agreement between the MISR aerosols product and AERONet measurements of AOD and ANG.
the MISR Version22 aerosol product can be improved by filtering the aerosol mixtures based on their agreement between ANG and AAOD values, and simulating the ANG and AA OD using the GOCART model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving the aerosol properties retrieved from satellite data.
the development of a new approach to improve the quality of satellite-retrieved microphysical aerosol properties by filtering the list MISR aerosol mixtures with the aid of GOCART model results.
improving satellite-retrieved microphysical properties using ground-based and model-derived information.

this study has shown that the MISR aerosols product is significantly improved when the GOCART data are used to filter the MISR aerosal mixtures.
the MISR Version 22 operational aerosol product is a useful tool for many applications.

The Multi-angle Imaging Spectroradiometer (MISR), which flies aboard the Terra satellite, is capable of providing reliable aerosol optical thickness (AOT) and better constraints of particle size (Angström exponent, or AN) and shape (sphericity), but the single scattering albedo (SS) is not well constrained.

the MISR Version-23 operational retrieval is improved by the application of GOCART constraints, especially for aerosol mixtures that are not constrained by the MISR retrieval algorithm.

the MISR aerosols are not well-constrained at lower AOD values.
the MISR aerosols optical depth (AOT) and Angstrom exponent (Ångström exponent) are not very good at low values of the AOT.
